subject: design/local-work-tracker-v2
statement: every mutation is a whole-file atomic replace — write a sibling temp file, `fsync`, then `rename()` over the target (atomic on POSIX) — and concurrent writes to *one* item are serialized by a per-item advisory lock (`flock`) held only across that read-modify-write. Reads take no lock: `rename()` guarantees a reader observes either the whole old file or the whole new one, never a torn one. **Reads that feed a destructive or dispatch decision** (readiness, closing, reaping) read the authoritative file directly and therefore reflect every prior write with no index or cache in the path (DINV-4 — AP-15/INV-7). Writes fail closed: a full disk or a failed `fsync` fails before the `rename`, leaving the prior file intact (AP-17). A crash mid-write leaves an orphaned temp file, swept on next run; the item is unharmed.
